To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we develop a new index that proxies for economic policy uncertainty; (ii) the index spikes at times when policy uncertainty is high; (iii) uncertainty has a negative impact on investment and employment; and (iv) policy uncertainty is a key factor in explaining the Great Recession.

(1) economic policy uncertainty is a useful new macroeconomic time series, (2) economic policy uncertainty has a negative effect on investment, employment, and output, (3) economic policy uncertainty rose sharply in the 1931-1933 period, (4) economic policy uncertainty increased substantially after 1960, and (5) economic policy uncertainty spiked in the 2010-2011 period.
Policy uncertainty, as measured by the frequency of newspaper coverage of economic policy issues, is an important macroeconomic variable that affects economic activity and stock market prices.
